newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila eyes early full oil industry deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Manila eyes early full oil industry deregulation.

text.p: The Philippines' Department of Energy said on Wednesday it will seek the approval of President Fidel Ramos to proceed with full deregulation of the oil industry by February 1996.

Energy Minister Francisco Viray told a news conference the department wants full deregulation a month earlier than scheduled since one billion pesos in the Oil Price Stabilisation Fund (OPSF) would be depleted by mid-February at the latest.
Under the deregulation law, full oil industry deregulation is scheduled on or before March 1997, subject to the approval of the President.

The OPSF is a buffer fund used to soften the impact of fluctuations in local oil prices. Since August last year, when the government partially deregulated the oil industry, oil prices have been adjusted monthly depending on Singapore Posted Prices.
Any increase over 50 centavos per litre was absorbed by the OPSF.
Viray said the one-billion-peso OPSF would have dwindled to 181 million pesos by mid-January.
With full deregulation, market forces will determine prices of petroleum products, Viray said.
